blocks.x: What Applied AI & GenAI changes inside Manufacturing & Industrial: the processes we target, the controls we inherit, the platforms underneath, and the measured delta at every gate.

In Manufacturing & Industrial, applied ai & generative ai at dataq soft covers the full lifecycle of enterprise intelligence: strategy and value mapping, platform build-out, model adaptation, retrieval architectures, multimodal systems, and the governance fabric that keeps every model auditable. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise ai strategy & roadmapping, generative ai platform engineering, llm fine-tuning & model operations — delivered on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Quality escapes and manual inspection

Defect detection depends on sampling and eyes; escapes reach customers, and scrap/rework costs hide in the P&L. Vision systems stall in pilot because lighting, thresholds and line integration were never engineered.
Brownfield instrumentation gap
Critical assets run uninstrumented because gut-and-replace is unthinkable; the data that twins and models need does not exist, and downtime for retrofit is unaffordable.
Planning by spreadsheet under volatility

Planners fight demand volatility, material shortages and changeovers in spreadsheets; scheduling knowledge lives in two veterans' heads. OEE losses from changeover and waiting are structurally accepted.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Below is the delivery cadence for this capability — the same pattern on every engagement. Weeks 1–2 measure and sign the baseline with your team; nothing builds against an unsigned number. Weeks 3–8 prove the pattern on deliberately bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — under a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, closing with a measured delta against the baseline. Every gate is pass, stop or redirect, in writing.
